boards.title: Your First Weekend at Texas A&M University-College Station, Shared as Cards
boards.description: A calm, walkable first-weekend sequence of campus landmarks, study stops, and public spaces.

cards.title: Start with campus orientation
cards.subtitle: Rudder Tower
cards.notes: Pick up campus context first, then use the Visitor Center’s landmarks list to set a simple walking route for the rest of the weekend.
cards.short_summary: Begin with an official overview of the campus.
cards.evidence_claim: Texas A&M’s Visitor Center identifies campus landmarks and points of interest, including the Memorial Student Center, Century Tree, and Academic Plaza.
cards.access_notes: Check the Visitor Center site before arrival for tour availability and visitor information.

cards.title: See the historic dome
cards.subtitle: Academic Plaza
cards.notes: Walk through Academic Plaza and pause at the rotunda details; the official campus guide notes both the seal mosaic and Liberty Bell replica.
cards.short_summary: A historic campus landmark with a distinctive rotunda.
cards.evidence_claim: The Academic Building was constructed in 1914 and its foyer includes a mosaic of Texas A&M’s seal and a Liberty Bell replica in the rotunda.
cards.access_notes: Use normal building-access rules; enjoy the exterior and plaza if interior access is limited.

cards.title: Walk to the Century Tree
cards.subtitle: Near the Academic Building
cards.notes: Continue a short distance to the live oak, take a photo from the path, and leave the tree and surrounding grounds undisturbed.
cards.short_summary: A named live-oak landmark beside Academic Plaza.
cards.evidence_claim: Texas A&M identifies the Century Tree as a live oak near the Academic Building, likely planted around the turn of the 20th century.
cards.access_notes: View from public campus paths and protect the tree’s root area.

cards.title: Browse the exhibition gallery
cards.subtitle: 400 Spence Street
cards.notes: Visit the first-floor exhibition gallery, then ask staff about current displays or arrange a tour if you want a deeper archives introduction.
cards.short_summary: An archives stop with a public exhibition gallery.
cards.evidence_claim: Cushing Memorial Library & Archives states that its first-floor exhibition gallery is open to the public and lists its address at 400 Spence Street.
cards.access_notes: The library’s visit page lists standard Monday–Friday hours; verify holiday and schedule changes before going.

cards.title: Follow Military Walk
cards.subtitle: Central campus walkway
cards.notes: Use this quarter-mile route to connect central-campus landmarks, reading the historical markers as you go instead of treating it as a hurried shortcut.
cards.short_summary: A marked pedestrian route through campus history.
cards.evidence_claim: Texas A&M describes Military Walk as a quarter-mile walkway through campus with historical markers and restored brick and limestone pavers.
cards.access_notes: Stay on the walkway and observe posted campus-access guidance.

cards.entity_name: Sam Houston Sanders Corps of Cadets Center
cards.title: Explore Corps history
cards.subtitle: Corps of Cadets area
cards.notes: Visit during posted weekday hours and focus on the museum exhibits, which document Corps history and several Texas A&M traditions.
cards.short_summary: A museum-based introduction to Corps and Aggie history.
cards.evidence_claim: The Sam Houston Sanders Corps of Cadets Center houses a museum with Aggie artifacts and exhibits on Texas A&M traditions and history.
cards.source_title: About Us | Texas A&M Corps of Cadets
cards.access_notes: The Corps site lists Monday–Friday, 8 a.m.–5 p.m.; confirm access before a weekend visit.

cards.title: Visit the Bonfire Memorial thoughtfully
cards.subtitle: Memorial site on campus
cards.notes: Walk the Spirit Ring slowly, read the portals and reflections, and keep the visit quiet and respectful of the people memorialized there.
cards.short_summary: A campus memorial interpreting the 1999 Bonfire collapse.
cards.evidence_claim: Texas A&M states that Bonfire Memorial was dedicated at the site of the 1999 Bonfire collapse and includes the Spirit Ring and 12 portals.
cards.access_notes: On-site tours are offered by MSC Hospitality; request one in advance if desired.

cards.title: Make the MSC your reset stop
cards.subtitle: 275 Joe Routt Boulevard
cards.notes: Use the MSC as a central indoor break: locate services, check event postings, and plan the next stop before heading back outside.
cards.short_summary: A central campus facility with services, vendors, and event spaces.
cards.evidence_claim: The Memorial Student Center hosts vendors, services, dining and entertainment, and lists its physical address at 275 Joe Routt Boulevard.
cards.source_title: Memorial Student Center | Texas A&M University
cards.access_notes: The page lists summer hours of 7 a.m.–8 p.m. Monday–Saturday and 10 a.m.–8 p.m. Sunday; verify seasonal hours.

cards.title: Take an outdoor pause at Aggie Park
cards.subtitle: Between Alumni Center and Koldus Building
cards.notes: Choose a bench or open lawn for a low-key break, then look for the water features and performance pavilion before continuing your walk.
cards.short_summary: A 20-acre campus park with water features and gathering space.
cards.evidence_claim: Texas A&M describes Aggie Park as a 20-acre outdoor space with an amphitheater, water features, an ice cream shop, and a performance pavilion.
cards.access_notes: Use public park areas and follow any event signage or temporary access restrictions.

cards.entity_name: The Gardens at Texas A&M University
cards.title: End with a daylight garden walk
cards.subtitle: 556 John Kimbrough Boulevard
cards.notes: Finish in daylight with a self-guided walk through the public gardens; take photos from paths and leave when it gets dark as requested.
cards.short_summary: A free public garden for a calm final stop.
cards.evidence_claim: The Gardens at Texas A&M are free to visit, open daily from dawn to dusk, and open to campus visitors and the public.
cards.source_title: Admission & Hours | The Gardens at Texas A&M University
cards.access_notes: Open daily from dawn to dusk; the Gardens asks visitors to leave when it gets dark.
